name: MEM1
ontology_notes: No external memory store. At each turn the agent writes a compact internal state IS_t that mixes reasoning and a summary of prior IS, query, and tool info, then prunes older tags from the prompt. Paper §3.1. Code Mem1/train/rollout/llm_agent/generation_think.py LLMGenerationManager._extract_think_and_response. Not user bio, character, relationship, lore, or OOC types.

ontology.evidence: IS_t is unstructured XML-tagged text in the prompt (paper §3). No tables or note types. generation_think.py stores the think span as reconstruction_list t{step}.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: The RL policy decides what to keep in the next IS. Paper §3.1 prunes prior tags after each turn. Algorithm 1 sets y <- y_t so previous context is removed. No user pin. No refusal of poisoned tool output except by learned discard.
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: Only the latest IS, query or answer, and current info stay in context (paper Fig. 2). Environment retrieve is a search or WebShop click, not a companion memory lookup. No silence gate.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: Each new IS replaces the previous prompt state. Paper §3.1. No fact-level invalid_at. A dropped detail is gone unless it was copied into the new IS.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Turns-left HINT is injected (paper §4.1). No dated memories or last-Tuesday queries.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: One shared IS for a web or QA agent. No user vs character vs relationship split.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Discard is for token budget and task success, not social skip of a relevant memory. Paper §1-3.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Tool info is concatenated into the next IS if the policy keeps it. No trust tags. Paper §5 notes the method needs verifiable rewards, not a poison filter.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: Default behavior drops prior observations after consolidation (paper Algorithm 1). That is working-memory eviction, not a user forget-that. MIT-MI/MEM1 issue 10 disputes whether training rollout matches that paper claim.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Paper Table 1 16-objective peak tokens 10.4 x 10^2 versus Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct 38.4 x 10^2. Abstract claims 3.5x task score and 3.7x less memory versus that 14B baseline. One policy LLM per turn. Extra cost is environment search (Faiss/E5 or Serper), not a second memory model.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: MIT LICENSE. Trained Qwen2.5-7B can run on one GPU after training. Training needs 4x H100/H200 (Appendix A.1). Online Web-QA uses Serper. Intimate chat is not the shipped loop.
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: Training and inference repo. No MCP server in MIT-MI/MEM1.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Long-horizon web and multi-hop QA agent. Memory is a learned prompt summary that discards. Still retrieve-or-search then speak. No companion types, silence, or poisoning controls. Do not clone the IS XML into a companion store.

published_eval.name: Composed multi-objective HotpotQA+Natural Questions (2 to 16 objectives), Wiki RAG, online web QA, WebShop
published_eval.claimed_score: MEM1-QA 16-objective EM 1.97 vs Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct 0.567, peak tokens about 3.7x lower (Table 1, abstract). WebShop avg final reward 70.87 vs AgentLM-7B 63.60 (Table 2).
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Exact match / F1 on interleaved multi-hop QA and WebShop purchase reward plus peak-token efficiency. Not companion identity, silence, or persona poisoning.

open_unknowns: Issue 10 claims training rollout truncates via kept_lengths and does not replace observations with internal_state the way §3 describes. Which path shipped in the Table 1 numbers is not settled from the paper alone.
Whether an IS trained on HotpotQA compositions can hold months of companion chat without a verifiable reward.
